clue.text: Very game, if muddled

indicators.note: if the word is muddled its letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is keen on a plan as long as it stays a bit confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang intensifier: 'mega rich' means very rich, so the informal adverb serves as an equivalent of extremely.

clue.text: Am I providing some examples with 4?

definitions.text: Am I providing some examples with 4?

parts.words: Am I providing some examples with 4?
parts.note: Am (americium) and I (iodine) are chemical symbols, and several substances that answer 4-down, such as neon or oxygen, are in the periodic table too

explanation.surface: A speaker wonders whether they are supplying instances to go with another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Am I' not as a question but as two chemical symbols, americium and iodine; the noble and other gases of 4-down join them in the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Americium, iodine and gases such as helium are all members of the periodic table of chemical substances.

clue.text: I'm pedantic about small creatures

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps around the other here

parts.note: anal, short for anal-retentive, describes someone fussily pedantic
taken as written, minus the apostrophe
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A fussy speaker confesses to being finicky about little beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm pedantic' reads as a confession, but 'about' is the container signal. The album of this name is one of the Pink Floyd themed entries.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: living beings such as beasts and pets are creatures, the plural noun matching the plural.

clue.text: Big man lost little 11 coming from here

indicators.note: lost means these letters are no longer there, taken out of the giant's name

parts.note: Goliath was the biblical giant slain by David
11-down is TWIST, as in Oliver Twist; little Oliver is the short form Oli

explanation.surface: A large man has misplaced a small dancing companion on the way here.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: the giant Goliath is described in the Bible as coming from this Philistine city.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical knowledge: Goliath is called 'of Gath', the Philistine city that was the giant's home town.

clue.text: Possibly noble when subordinate to German leader

indicators.note: in a down answer, being subordinate puts this piece below the other one
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: Someone might be of aristocratic rank while serving under a German head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noble' suggests aristocracy, but it is chemistry: helium, neon and argon are the noble ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: neon, argon and the rest are called noble because they barely react, so such a substance may be noble.

clue.text: Now, some thoughts about trouper's philosophy

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shares a few reflections on a theatrical performer's outlook on life.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a Queen song and also a track on Pink Floyd's The Wall, tying both themes together.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a seasoned performer carries on whatever happens, and this saying sums up that stage creed.

clue.text: Digression that's on record (like 31 of any colour you like?)

definitions.meaning: a remark made in passing, off the main subject

definitions.text: on record (like 31 of any colour you like?)
definitions.meaning: the main track of a single; Pink Floyd's Money was issued with Any Colour You Like on the flip

explanation.surface: A rambling aside about vinyl and a famous single from Dark Side of the Moon.
explanation.walkthrough: Money (31) was the main track of a 1973 Pink Floyd single whose flip was Any Colour You Like.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a remark spoken in passing; the other is the main track of a vinyl single.

clue.text: Violinist's exhortation to abolish the monarchy?

parts.note: to scrap something is to abolish it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen and so the crown

explanation.surface: A fiddler urges the end of royal rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 's exhortation' frames the wordplay as a command to scrap ER, with ER being the Queen, which nods to the band Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogatory slang: a poor fiddler is said to scrape the strings, so a violinist can be called a scraping player.

clue.text: Empty debate? A swizz, according to clergyman

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its inside, keeping just its outer letters

parts.note: a swizz is a swindle, a con

explanation.surface: A churchman calls a hollow argument a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: John Deacon was Queen's bass player.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an ordained minister ranking below a priest is a clergyman of that order.

clue.text: Some countries dropping bar for all that remain

indicators.note: dropping means letting this piece fall out of the longer word

parts.note: republics are countries without a monarch, so only some countries
a pub is a bar

explanation.surface: A few nations abolish their drinking dens.
explanation.walkthrough: Relics is also a Pink Floyd compilation album.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: relics are the surviving remnants of something, everything left behind.

clue.text: Timeless times: being inside, being outside

indicators.note: being inside tells us the multiplication piece sits within the other word

parts.note: something timeless lasts for ever, eternal
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A paradoxical riddle about eternity, being in and being out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an exterior thing lies on the outside, the opposite of internal.

clue.text: Dance, pervert!

definitions.meaning: a 1960s dance made famous by Chubby Checker
to pervert is to distort, warp the meaning of

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at someone on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a 1960s dance craze; the other is to distort or warp something, as a meaning.

clue.text: She has some leverage

indicators.note: the word has some of these letters within it, hiding a name

explanation.surface: A woman holds a bit of bargaining power.
explanation.walkthrough: Vera is a song on Pink Floyd's The Wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a woman's name, so it can stand for any she.

clue.text: Bishop's cry of recognition — one having faith

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
aha is what one exclaims on realising something
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bishop exclaims as he spots a fellow believer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the term names a follower of the religion founded by Baha'u'llah, someone holding that faith.

clue.text: One's surrounded by lies again

indicators.note: surrounded by tells us the numeral sits within the other piece

parts.note: BS, short for bullshit, is slang for lies
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is once more caught in a web of untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical term: written on a score, this Latin word asks for a passage to be played twice, a second time.

clue.text: Stay forward

definitions.meaning: a stay is a support or brace
in rugby a front-row forward is called this

explanation.surface: Remain in front.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a support holding something up; the other is a front-row player in a rugby scrum.

clue.text: I never went in for siestas — dreadful standstills!

indicators.note: the speaker never went in, so that letter stays out of the mix
dreadful signals that the letters are rearranged badly

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that afternoon naps were never for them, awful periods of inactivity.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I out of SIESTAS and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: stases are states of equilibrium or inactivity, halts where nothing moves.

clue.text: Assume donkey's killed returning bird

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so what remains is read backwards
killed means this animal is removed from the word

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone takes for granted that a donkey was slain by a bird on its way back.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the large flightless Australian runner is a bird.

clue.text: Start to wonder at tigers: half were destroyed by floods

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
the first half of the word is gone, leaving the second half

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at tigers, half of which were wiped out in a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger Waters was Pink Floyd's bassist.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: inundations of rising water are floods.

clue.text: Molecular core kind of 31

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A science writer describes the heart of a molecule as a type of currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the European Currency Unit was a basket currency, a type of money before the euro.

clue.text: Roam about, single, deserted, stranded

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around into a new order

parts.note: single means one
D is the abbreviation for deserted in military records

explanation.surface: A list of a lonely wanderer's states: roaming, alone, abandoned, stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: Marooned is a Pink Floyd instrumental.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone left on a desert island is stranded with no way off.

clue.text: Chairman reported twice on Kenyan activists

indicators.note: twice means the piece appears two times
reported means as spoken aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Chairman Mao Zedong led communist China

explanation.surface: News of a Chinese leader appears in a report about Kenyan rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: History: the Mau Mau were insurgents fighting British colonial rule in Kenya in the 1950s.

clue.text: When are unusual outsiders imprisoned? Generally

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'

indicators.note: imprisoned means held inside the other word
the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A question asking when the edges of something odd get locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase means usually, in most cases, which is what generally says too.

clue.text: Graduate's working for builder

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate; the 's adds S
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A university leaver takes a job as a builder.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Mason is Pink Floyd's drummer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stonemason is a craftsman who builds with stone.

clue.text: Mother greeted by sound of cheers in state capital

indicators.note: greeted by means the next piece follows the first

parts.note: mum is mother

indicators.note: sound of means a word that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: cheers is British slang for goodbye, bye

explanation.surface: A mother is welcomed with applause in an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Geography: the city formerly called Bombay is the capital of the Indian state of Maharashtra.

clue.text: Can take nothing out of county

indicators.note: take, completed by out of, means removing a piece
out of finishes the instruction to remove the letter from the word

parts.note: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to remove zero from a county.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the modal verb expressing permission, as in 'you can go' or 'you may go'.

clue.text: Like Andrew, holding copper or another metal

indicators.note: holding means one word contains the other

parts.note: a merry-andrew is a clown, so Andrew is merry
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Something like Andrew, containing copper or a different element.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: quicksilver is a liquid metal, distinct from the copper already in the clue.

clue.text: Starts to query undertaking as neuroscientists try to set up body

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their opening letters

parts.note: to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Scientists studying the brain question a project while trying to establish an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: British usage: a quasi-autonomous non-governmental organisation is a body created by government but run at arm's length.

clue.text: Others left books out in restaurant to create atmosphere

indicators.note: left means departed, so this piece goes away
out means taken away from the word

parts.note: the whole word restaurant is the fodder; that its middle letters happen to read as the answer is a coincidence of the deletion
the rest are the others
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Diners forget their books in an eatery, giving the place a certain ambience.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the distinctive feeling or ambience surrounding a person or place.

clue.text: Volunteers within state get something to eat

indicators.note: within means inside the other word

parts.note: to state is to say
TA is the Territorial Army, the British army's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers in a state are fed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: grilled skewered meat with peanut sauce is a dish to eat.

clue.text: Use deceit to get money out of castle

definitions.text: Use deceit to get money out of

definitions.meaning: in chess, the piece also called a castle

explanation.surface: Swindling cash out of a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to cheat someone of money; the other is the chess piece also called a castle.

clue.text: If nothing needs underlining initially, object to finally providing hint

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letters

parts.note: an end is an object or aim

indicators.note: finally means the last letter

explanation.surface: A writer reasons that unemphasised text eventually provides a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an indirect suggestive remark is a hint or insinuation.

clue.text: Do vessels have changes of direction

parts.note: ut was the old name for the first note of the scale, now do or doh
urns are vessels

explanation.surface: A question about whether ships alter course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the start of a question but is the musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: complete reversals of course, turning back the way one came.

clue.text: It's revolting taking part in bug hunt

indicators.note: taking part in means part of these words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Searching for insects is disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclamation of disgust, what one says on finding something revolting.

clue.text: Second to back Japanese currency — and others

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second

indicators.note: to back means read backwards

parts.note: the Japanese currency unit is the yen

explanation.surface: A second person backs the yen and other currencies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japanese currency' looks like one phrase, but currency belongs to the definition. Money is a Pink Floyd track.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cash in any denomination, yen and every other currency.

clue.text: Main character has to move slowly

indicators.note: has means the words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: The protagonist needs to proceed at a crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to edge forward a little at a time, creeping along.

clue.text: My good man, every other character is one with idiosyncratic syntax

indicators.note: every other character means alternate letters

explanation.surface: A teacher addresses a man whose grammar is odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Film knowledge: the Star Wars Jedi master speaks with inverted word order, as in 'strong you are'.
